subject.title: Bug: Billing error (402) causes infinite retry death spiral for inline-apiKey providers (no backoff)

question: Should OpenClaw accept persisted provider-scoped cooldown state for inline provider API keys as the long-term behavior for this issue?
rationale: The source bug is clear, but the fix intentionally changes inline-key runtime behavior to fail closed during billing/auth cooldown windows and affects auth-provider compatibility.

options.title: Accept provider-scoped cooldown
options.body: Proceed with the linked fix path after rebase and review so inline keys participate in the existing cooldown contract.

options.title: Request a narrower compatibility shape
options.body: Ask for a design that preserves current inline-key behavior by default or limits the persisted cooldown impact.

options.title: Document auth profiles only
options.body: Decline core inline-key cooldown and steer users to auth profiles plus cooldown config.

recommendation.title: Accept provider-scoped cooldown
recommendation.body: Proceed with the linked fix path after rebase and review so inline keys participate in the existing cooldown contract.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent provider-auth warmup and auth-profile usage history makes this the strongest routing candidate for the compatibility-sensitive auth decision.
